chunks: Title: Billing and Payment FAQ Category: Billing Common billing questions and their answers. Q: Why is my bill higher than usual? A: Common reasons include: plan upgrade mid-cycle (prorated charges), late payment fee (applied after 15 days past due date), one-time installation or equipment charges, or taxes/regulatory fees adjustment. Check the bill breakdown in your customer portal under "My Bills." Q: How do I pay my bill? A: You can pay through the customer portal using credit/debit card, bank transfer, or JazzCash/EasyPaisa. Auto-pay can be enabled in account settings. Q: When is my bill due? A: Bills are generated on the 1st of each month and are due by the 15th. A grace period of 5 additional days is provided before late fees apply. Service may be suspended after 30 days of non-payment. Q: I paid but it still shows unpaid. A: Bank transfers can take 1-3 business days to reflect. If payment was made via portal, it should reflect within 24 hours. If the issue persists after 3 business days, contact support with your payment receipt or transaction ID. Q: How do I change my plan? A: Plan changes can be requested through the portal or by contacting support. Upgrades take effect immediately with prorated billing. Downgrades take effect at the start of the next billing cycle. Q: I want a refund for downtime. A: If you experienced a verified outage lasting more than 24 consecutive hours, you may be eligible for a prorated credit. Contact support with the dates of the outage and a credit will be applied to your next bill after verification.

Title: New Connection Installation Guide Category: Installation Everything about getting a new internet connection installed. Installation timeline: - Urban areas: 2-3 business days after order confirmation. - Suburban areas: 3-5 business days. - Rural areas: 5-10 business days (may require additional infrastructure). What to expect on installation day: 1. A technician will visit your premises at the scheduled time (a 2-hour window will be communicated). 2. Someone over 18 must be present at the address to authorize the installation. 3. The technician will install the fiber/cable entry point, set up the router, and test the connection. 4. Installation typically takes 1-2 hours. Requirements for installation: - Valid government ID of the account holder. - Access to the building's cable entry point (for apartments, coordinate with building management). - A power outlet near the desired router location. - The first month's bill and installation fee must be paid before the visit. After installation: - Default WiFi name and password are on the sticker under your router. - Change the default password through the router admin panel (192.168.1.1) for security. - Download the NetDesk app to manage your account, pay bills, and contact support. Rescheduling or cancelling: - You can reschedule up to 24 hours before the appointment through the portal or by calling support. - If you're not present during the scheduled visit, a rescheduling fee may apply.

Title: Network Outage Information Category: NetworkOutage How to identify and respond to network outages. Signs of a network outage vs a local issue: - If ONLY your connection is down and neighbors have internet, it's likely a local issue (router, cable, or account problem). - If multiple people in your area report no internet, it's likely a network outage. - If the router's "Internet/WAN" light is red or off, but "Power" and "LAN" lights are normal, it's likely an upstream issue. What to do during a confirmed outage: 1. Check the NetDesk portal or app for outage notifications in your area. 2. Do NOT repeatedly restart your router — this won't help during an outage and may cause configuration issues. 3. If you need urgent internet access, consider using mobile hotspot as a temporary solution. 4. Outages are typically resolved within 2-6 hours. Major infrastructure outages may take up to 24 hours. What our team does during an outage: - Network Operations Center (NOC) is automatically alerted when multiple customers in an area go offline. - Field teams are dispatched if the issue is physical infrastructure (cable cuts, equipment failure). - Software/configuration issues are resolved remotely by the NOC team. After an outage is resolved: - Your connection should restore automatically. If it doesn't within 30 minutes of the outage being marked resolved, restart your router once. - If service doesn't return after restart, contact support — your connection may need manual re-provisioning.

Title: How to Reset Your Router Category: NetworkOutage, SlowSpeed If your internet connection has dropped or is extremely slow, a router reset is the first step to try. Step 1: Unplug the power cable from the back of your router. Do NOT press the reset button — that factory-resets the device and erases your settings. Step 2: Wait exactly 30 seconds. This allows the router's memory to fully clear and the ISP connection to properly drop. Step 3: Plug the power cable back in. Wait 2-3 minutes for all lights to stabilize. The "Internet" or "WAN" light should turn solid green. Step 4: Test your connection by opening a website on your phone or computer. If the issue persists, try connecting with an ethernet cable directly to rule out WiFi problems. If the router still shows a red or blinking "Internet" light after 5 minutes, this may indicate an outage in your area or a line fault. Contact support for further diagnosis. Common mistakes: Using the reset pinhole button (this factory-resets the router), not waiting long enough, restarting the computer instead of the router.

Title: Diagnosing Slow Internet Speed Category: SlowSpeed If your internet feels slow, follow these diagnostic steps before contacting support. Step 1: Run a speed test at speedtest.net or fast.com. Note your download speed, upload speed, and ping. Compare these to your subscribed plan speed. Step 2: If speeds are below 50% of your plan, disconnect all other devices from WiFi and test again. Other devices streaming video or downloading files consume bandwidth. Step 3: Test with an ethernet cable directly connected to the router. If wired speed is normal but WiFi is slow, the issue is WiFi interference, not your internet connection. Step 4: Check if the issue is time-dependent. Speeds dropping in the evening (7-11 PM) suggest network congestion in your area, which may require a plan upgrade or network optimization by our team. Step 5: Check your router's age. Routers older than 3-4 years may not support modern WiFi standards (WiFi 5/6) and can bottleneck your connection even if the line speed is fine. WiFi interference causes: Microwave ovens, baby monitors, Bluetooth devices, neighboring WiFi networks on the same channel, thick walls or floors between router and device. When to escalate: If wired speed is consistently below 50% of plan speed at multiple times of day, this indicates a line or network issue requiring technician investigation.

Title: WiFi Connectivity Troubleshooting Category: SlowSpeed, NetworkOutage Fixing common WiFi problems when your internet line is actually working fine. Problem: Device won't connect to WiFi - Forget the network on your device and reconnect with the password. - Check if the router's WiFi light is on. If not, press the WiFi button on the router. - Check if your device is trying to connect to the 5GHz band — some older devices only support 2.4GHz. - Restart your device. Problem: WiFi keeps disconnecting - Move closer to the router. Thick walls, metal objects, and floors significantly weaken signal. - Switch from 5GHz to 2.4GHz band. 5GHz is faster but has shorter range. - Check if the router is overheating. Ensure it has ventilation and isn't stacked on other electronics. - Update your device's WiFi drivers (for laptops). Problem: WiFi is slow but wired connection is fast - This confirms the issue is WiFi, not your internet line. - Change the WiFi channel in router settings (192.168.1.1). Channels 1, 6, and 11 have least interference on 2.4GHz. - Consider a WiFi extender or mesh system for large homes. - Position the router centrally in your home, elevated, and away from walls. Problem: Some devices work but others don't - Check if the non-working device has a MAC address that might be blocked in router settings. - Check if the device's IP address conflicts with another device. Restart the router to reassign IPs. - Try connecting the problem device to a mobile hotspot to confirm the device's WiFi hardware works.
